partners.mechanism_chain: MED12 (HGNC:7066) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of transcription and chromatin remodeling (GO:0006351); Regulation of transcription and chromatin remodeling (GO:0006351) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Regulation of transcription and chromatin remodeling (GO:0006351) —LEADS_TO→ Marfanoid habitus (HP:0001070); ACADM (HGNC:6) —DISRUPTS→ Fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0015986); Fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0015986) —DECREASES→ Medium-chain acylcarnitines (CHEBI:23703); Medium-chain acylcarnitines (CHEBI:23703) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0012298); Medium-chain acylcarnitines (CHEBI:23703) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Regulation of transcription and chromatin remodeling (GO:0006351) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0012298). Loss of function of MED12 disrupts transcriptional regulation and chromatin remodeling, leading to intellectual disability and marfanoid habitus. Concurrently, loss of function of ACADM impairs fatty acid beta-oxidation, causing accumulation of medium-chain acylcarnitines. This metabolic derangement contributes to encephalopathy, hypotonia, and can indirectly affect neuronal development and function, converging with the effects of MED12 dysfunction on neuronal integrity and resulting in overlapping phenotypes like intellectual disability and hypotonia.

partners.mechanism_chain: MED12 (HGNC:7034) —DISRUPTS→ PPAR signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-6797086); PPAR signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-6797086) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); PPARG (HGNC:9294) —DISRUPTS→ PPAR signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-6797086); PPAR signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-6797086) —LEADS_TO→ Type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148). Loss-of-function mutations in MED12 disrupt the normal functioning of the PPAR signaling pathway, contributing to intellectual disability in XLID-M. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in genes like PPARG, which also regulate the PPAR signaling pathway, contribute to the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus. The shared convergence on the PPAR signaling pathway provides a mechanistic link between these two diseases.

partners.mechanism_chain: LEP (HGNC:6570) —BINDS→ Leptin-melanocortin signaling pathway (GO:0030521); LEPR (HGNC:6571) —BINDS→ Leptin-melanocortin signaling pathway (GO:0030521); Leptin-melanocortin signaling pathway (GO:0030521) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Leptin-melanocortin signaling pathway (GO:0030521) —LEADS_TO→ Obesity (HP:0005101); POMC (HGNC:9199) —PRODUCES→ Leptin-melanocortin signaling pathway (GO:0030521); PCSK1 (HGNC:9573) —DISRUPTS→ POMC (HGNC:9199); PPARG (HGNC:9295) —BINDS→ Adipogenesis and energy homeostasis (GO:0006629); Adipogenesis and energy homeostasis (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Obesity (HP:0005101). Mutations in LEP, LEPR, POMC, PCSK1, and PPARG can disrupt the leptin-melanocortin signaling pathway and adipogenesis/energy homeostasis pathways, leading to both intellectual disability and obesity. For example, loss-of-function mutations in LEP or LEPR lead to impaired leptin signaling, affecting appetite regulation and potentially brain development. Similarly, mutations in POMC or PCSK1 disrupt the production or processing of melanocortins, impacting energy balance and neurodevelopment. PPARG mutations affect adipogenesis and metabolic regulation, contributing to obesity and potentially other developmental phenotypes.
